speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand the onset and progression, how many days ago did these symptoms first begin, and has anyone around you been sick recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, preceded by a low-grade viral illness, followed by a characteristic "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, is classic for this condition caused by Parvovirus B19. No further testing is required as the diagnosis is clinically evident.
